name: gke-plan-run-dispatch
description: Dispatching plan-runs against the live GKE warren (app.warren.run): export WARREN_BASE_URL=https://app.warren.run and WARREN_API_TOKEN from 'kubectl get secret warren-secrets -n warren -o jsonpath={.data.warren-api-token} | base64 -d' (context gke_warren-502318_us-west1_warren). Push seeds/plan changes to origin main FIRST, then POST /projects/prj_dp15vt7h8f4v/refresh to advance the server clone, then 'warren plan run <pl-id> --project prj_dp15vt7h8f4v --agent claude-code --ref main --no-follow'. Coordinator skips closed children on resume (verified: pl-3a79 resumed at warren-b8bf after 7 closed children). Adopt-only plans (sd plan create + sd plan adopt) group existing stray seeds into a dispatchable plan with zero new child seeds.

title: Public instance uses a repo-granular allowlist, not a bare owner
rationale: A bare 'jayminwest' owner entry would authorize the private trellis repo and every future private repo. The boot assertion would still pass today because trellis is not registered, so the short form looks safe now and fails open later. Storing both values as warren-secrets keys rather than literal manifest values makes reverting the auth posture a kubectl patch plus a rollout restart instead of a commit, release and deploy — the auth posture is the one setting an operator may need to revert in seconds.

name: live-public-instance-verification
description: Verifying a public warren deployment is a two-part job, because scenario 39 CANNOT be pointed at a live instance — it boots its own warren on a temp root with a seeded database, which is what makes it cheap enough for CI. Part one: confirm the acceptance-public workflow passed on the EXACT deployed SHA. Part two: run an anonymous live probe that (a) enumerates blocked routes from API_ROUTE_POLICIES, the same source of truth scenario 39 uses, so it cannot drift from a hand-written list; (b) fills path params from real ids discovered off the live instance, so nothing passes vacuously on a 404; (c) greps readable bodies for credential-SHAPED patterns rather than literals. Matching the bare word 'Bearer' produces false positives — agent prompt text legitimately contains 'Bearer $WARREN_API_TOKEN' as an unexpanded shell variable — so require a token-shaped tail. Also check the served SPA shell and its JS bundle, which no server-side projection covers.

kubectl apply -k on the gke-live overlay clobbered the imperatively-created warren-openrouter-key Secret with its secrets.yaml REPLACE_ME stub: any NEW stub added to deploy/k8s/base/secrets.yaml must also get a $patch:delete entry in deploy/k8s/overlays/gke/kustomization.yaml (the existing warren-secrets / warren-git-token entries are that guard).
resolution: Added the $patch:delete entry for warren-openrouter-key to the gke overlay (PR #681) and restored the live value with kubectl patch --patch-file, which preserves the last-applied annotation; the secret value was piped from .env.deployed via shell substitution so it never entered logs or context.
